paper_metadata.title: Quantum state preparation for multivariate functions

summary: The paper develops an LCU-based gate-model method for preparing multivariate quantum states from Fourier or Chebyshev series, with asymptotic two-qubit cost O(dD + Dn log d) for Fourier and O(dD + Ddn log n) for Chebyshev. It demonstrates noiseless simulations for a 2D Ricker wavelet and a bivariate Student’s t-distribution, and a hardware run on Quantinuum H2-1 for a 2D Gaussian using 24 qubits, achieving fidelities of 0.986 (uncorrelated) and 0.918 (correlated) with 80 and 237 two-qubit gates, respectively.

experiments.description: Preparation of a 2D Ricker wavelet on a 24-qubit grid using a Chebyshev-series state-preparation circuit, evaluated in noiseless simulation across multiple degrees and grid sizes.

algorithm.variant: LCU-based multivariate state preparation with Chebyshev series

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each variable discretized on n qubits; Chebyshev basis functions block-encoded with additional ancilla register of size b=ceil(log2 n); coefficients loaded via LCU ancilla register of size a=ceil(log2(d+1))
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare a quantum state with amplitudes proportional to a discretized approximation of the 2D Ricker wavelet f(x,y)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Chebyshev interpolation on the domain [-1,1]^2; coefficients computed via FFT/DCT from sampled values
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Maximum absolute error over grid points and over the continuous domain; gate counts from compiled circuits; success probability from noiseless simulation

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Chebyshev coefficients computed by interpolation/FFT; target function sampled on Chebyshev roots
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Rescaling of simulated amplitudes for comparison; numerical global optimization for continuous-domain error bound

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: error decreases rapidly with degree; supergeometric convergence until machine precision

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic speedup claim is made; the paper reports resource scaling and numerical accuracy only.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(dD + Ddn log n) two-qubit gates for Chebyshev approach
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(dx dy log(dx dy)) for 2D coefficient computation via FFT/DCT; more generally O(d^D log d) preprocessing for multivariate FFT-based coefficient extraction

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper reports asymptotic gate scaling O(dD + Ddn log n) and a noiseless simulation study, but no classical runtime comparison or end-to-end advantage benchmark.
limiting_factors: State-preparation success probability is < 1 and depends on post-selection

notes: Hardware is a noiseless simulation of circuits compiled for Quantinuum H2-1; the paper reports 24 qubits for the hardware experiment and 30 qubits for the largest simulated circuit in the Ricker-wavelet study.
Circuit depth is not explicitly tabulated for this experiment, so it is left null/inferred only at a high level from compiled gate counts.
No asymptotic speedup claim is made; the paper provides resource scaling only.
The paper presents a resource analysis and noiseless simulation for a 2D Ricker wavelet, not a quantum advantage claim.

experiments.description: Preparation of a bivariate Student’s t-distribution using a 2D Fourier-series state-preparation circuit, evaluated in noiseless simulation across multiple degrees and grid sizes.

algorithm.variant: LCU-based multivariate state preparation with Fourier series

hyperparameters.periodic_extension: mirror on [0,1]^2 then extend periodically with period 2

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each variable discretized on n qubits over [0,1]; Fourier basis functions implemented by phase-shift block-encodings; coefficient register size a=ceil(log2(2d+1)) per dimension
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare a quantum state with amplitudes proportional to a discretized Fourier approximation of the bivariate Student's t-distribution

problem_instance.description: Bivariate non-standardized Student's t-distribution with one degree of freedom (Cauchy)
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Periodic extension from [0,1]^2 to [-1,1]^2 via mirroring; Fourier coefficients computed by FFT on sampled grid
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Maximum absolute error over grid points and continuous-domain upper bound; gate counts from compiled circuits; success probability from noiseless simulation

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Fourier coefficients computed by FFT after periodic extension
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Rescaling of simulated amplitudes for comparison; numerical global optimization for continuous-domain error bound

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: error decays approximately as O(1/d) due to derivative discontinuity from periodic extension

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic speedup claim is made; the paper reports resource scaling and numerical accuracy only.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(dD + Dn log d) two-qubit gates for Fourier approach
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(dx dy log(dx dy)) for 2D FFT coefficient computation; more generally O(d^D log d) preprocessing

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper reports asymptotic gate scaling O(dD + Dn log d) and noiseless simulation results, but no classical baseline or advantage claim.
limiting_factors: Accuracy depends on Fourier approximation quality and periodic extension

notes: The paper reports compiled two-qubit gate counts and qubit counts (e.g. 26 qubits for the largest Student's t experiment) but not a single explicit circuit depth for this experiment.
No asymptotic speedup claim is made; only resource scaling and empirical accuracy are reported.
The paper reports resource scaling and approximation error behavior, not a quantum advantage result.

experiments.description: Preparation of 3D single-electron wavefunctions in a periodic Coulomb potential using a Fourier-series state-preparation circuit, evaluated by statevector simulation for ground and first excited states.

algorithm.variant: Fourier-series state preparation for first-quantized electronic wavefunctions

hyperparameters.unit_cell: (1x1x1) periodic Coulomb potential with one nucleus at center

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Three spatial dimensions discretized on n qubits each; Fourier coefficients loaded with ancilla registers of size a per dimension; state prepared on 3n main qubits plus 3a ancillas
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare wavefunctions psi(r)=sum_k c_k e^{i pi k^T r} for a single electron in a periodic Coulomb potential

problem_instance.description: Single electron in a 3D translationally invariant Coulomb potential in a periodic unit cell
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Coefficients obtained by solving the time-independent Schrödinger equation in a plane-wave basis
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Statevector simulation compared against direct numerical evaluation of the wavefunction; resource counts compiled for varying n and a

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Solve electronic structure linear system for Fourier coefficients
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Direct comparison of simulated probability densities to exact numerical densities

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic speedup claim is made; the paper reports resource scaling and numerical agreement with direct evaluation.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(dD + Dn log d) two-qubit gates for Fourier approach
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical solution of the discretized Schrödinger equation; exact asymptotic complexity not stated in the paper

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper reports compiled resource counts for 3D wavefunction preparation (e.g. 30 qubits and 1656 two-qubit gates for one setting) but no classical comparison.
limiting_factors: Resource cost grows with coefficient-register size

notes: The paper reports total qubits for the 30-qubit case (3n+3a) and compiled gate counts in Table 2, but not a single explicit depth value for the wavefunction experiments.
The classical solver is the Schrödinger-equation coefficient computation, which is part of preprocessing rather than a separate experiment.
This is a state-preparation demonstration for electronic wavefunctions, not an advantage benchmark.

experiments.description: Hardware demonstration of 2D Gaussian state preparation on Quantinuum H2-1 trapped-ion hardware for both uncorrelated and correlated Gaussians, using a Fourier-series state-preparation circuit and 20,000 shots per setting.

algorithm.variant: LCU-based multivariate state preparation with Fourier series on hardware

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two-dimensional Fourier-series approximation on 9 qubits per spatial dimension; coefficient registers of 3 qubits per dimension; post-selection on ancillas
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare a quantum state whose amplitudes encode a 2D Gaussian density (or its absolute value) on a 512x512 grid
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection on ancillas in |0>; for readout comparison, magnitudes |fd(x,y)| are used

problem_instance.description: Uncorrelated and correlated 2D Gaussian distributions on [0,1]^2
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Fourier coefficients computed analytically from the Gaussian characteristic function after extending the density to zero outside [0,1]^2; kernel density estimation used for post-processing of measurement data
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 20,000 shots per setting; compare KDE-estimated densities and marginals to target; compute mean, variance, correlation, and fidelity

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Analytic Fourier coefficients from Gaussian characteristic function; kernel density estimation with cross-validation for output analysis
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Rescale KDE-estimated densities to compare with target; compute fidelities and moments

speedup_claims.caveats: No speedup claim is made; this is a hardware demonstration of state preparation and output characterization.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(dD + Dn log d) two-qubit gates for Fourier approach
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Analytic coefficient computation plus KDE post-processing; exact asymptotic complexity not stated

notes: The paper explicitly reports 24 qubits, 237 two-qubit gates for the correlated case, 80 two-qubit gates for the uncorrelated case, and depth 42 for the uncorrelated full state-preparation circuit; the correlated circuit depth is 352 in Appendix C.2.
The experiment uses real Quantinuum H2-1 hardware with 20,000 shots per setting.
No asymptotic speedup claim is made.

experiments.description: Hardware demonstration of preparing a 2D Gaussian distribution on the Quantinuum H2-1 trapped-ion quantum computer using a Fourier-series state-preparation circuit, for both uncorrelated and correlated cases.

algorithm.variant: LCU-based multivariate state preparation with Fourier series

key_results: Uncorrelated case: 80 two-qubit gates, depth 42, fidelity F = 0.986
Correlated case: 237 two-qubit gates, depth 352, fidelity F = 0.918
Success probabilities from noiseless simulation: 0.134 (correlated) and 0.139 (uncorrelated)
Executed on Quantinuum H2-1 trapped-ion quantum computer with 20,000 shots
